name: Baron Bertram Graywater
oracle_text:
Whenever one or more tokens you control enter, create a 1/1 black Vampire Rogue creature token with lifelink. This ability triggers only once each turn.
{1}{B}, Sacrifice another creature or artifact: Draw a card.
blocked_sentences: Whenever one or more tokens you control enter, create a 1/1 black Vampire Rogue creature token with lifelink. This ability triggers only once each turn.

needs.what: a per-turn cap on a triggered ability, declared on the trigger itself -- e.g. `"trigger": {"event": "permanent_enters", "filter": {"is_token": true, "controller": "you"}, "max_per_turn": 1}` -- so that once the ability has triggered that many times this turn, later matching events do not queue it at all. It must be counted in `triggers.collect`/`_matches` per (source object, ability index) against the turn ledger, reset at cleanup, and it must be a *trigger*-count cap, not a resolution-count one: a trigger that was countered or removed from the stack still spends the turn's allowance
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `TriggerSpec`/`TriggerModel` are strict models with only `event`, `controller`, `source`, `filter`, `condition`, `defending`, `not_cause` and `counter` -- there is no per-turn limiter, so the trigger fires on every matching event. The two near misses both say something different. `set_flag`/`{"has_flag": ...}` is a one-way word (`objects.py` clears `flags` only on a zone change, never at end of turn), so it would make this once *ever* rather than once each turn. `{"cmp": {"left": {"resolutions_this_turn": true}, ...}}` is the engine's "Do this only once each turn" (Deep Gnome Terramancer wording): `ctx.resolutions` is set by `stack.resolve_top` and counts resolutions of the ability, so the trigger still goes on the stack every time and a countered or fizzled first copy would leave the allowance unspent -- the printed line here restricts triggering, not resolving

needs.what: a way to say "whenever one or more <matching> permanents enter" -- one trigger for a whole simultaneous batch of ENTERS_BATTLEFIELD events rather than one per object. Needs the entering permanents to be gathered into a single event (or the queued triggers deduplicated per batch) before `collect` queues anything, with the batch exposed as a binding so an effect can still read how many entered
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `permanent_enters` maps one-to-one onto `EventType.ENTERS_BATTLEFIELD` and `triggers.fire` is called once per object, so a `{"is_token": true, "controller": "you"}` filter queues N copies when N tokens enter together -- an anthem-style token maker would make N Vampires instead of one. `not_cause` only suppresses a trigger by cause and `condition` is evaluated per event, so neither can collapse a batch

needs.what: a `vampire_rogue_1_1_b_lifelink` token in `data/cards/tokens.cards.json` -- a 1/1 black Creature -- Vampire Rogue with lifelink -- for `create_token` to name
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `loader.validate_token_references` refuses to load any card whose `create_token` names a token that is not in the pool, and the pool's nearest token, `vampire_1_1_b_lifelink`, has subtypes `["Vampire"]` only. Using it would print the wrong type line and silently drop the Rogue subtype that Rogue-tribal cards read. A card answer file defines one card and cannot add a token definition, so this has to come from an /extend-dsl run -- the same route `clue_token` took for Bygone Bishop
